summary: Documents the composition, selection, roles and organization of the Internet Architecture Board. It replaces RFC 1601. It is a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: This is the rule book for a group of advisors who watch over how the Internet is designed. It says who sits on the group, how they are picked and what they do.

subtitle: The rules for who sits on the Internet Architecture Board, how they are chosen and what the board does.

tldr.problem: The IAB needed a current written charter covering its membership, roles and way of working, with material that other documents now cover removed from the old one.
tldr.mechanism: The charter sets a board of thirteen full members, lists its responsibilities from IESG appointment to architectural oversight, and defines its chair, decision rule and openness practices.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 1601, adds liaison seats for the Internet Society and the IANA, and describes how decisions are made when unanimity is not possible.

facts.label: Sitting member terms
facts.value: Six appointed each year for two years

facts.label: Quorum to act
facts.value: At least seven full members concur, no more than two dissents

today: RFC 2850 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 39) that replaced RFC 1601 and has been updated by RFC 9283.

sections.title: Who Is on the IAB
sections.content:
The Internet Architecture Board (IAB) has thirteen full members: the chair of the IETF plus twelve sitting members. The IETF chair, who also chairs the IESG, can take part in all official IAB actions except approving IESG members and appeals against IESG decisions.

Members serve as individuals, not as representatives of any company, agency or other organization, and owe no fiduciary duty of loyalty or care to the IAB, IETF, IRTF or IESG.

Full members are selected under the procedures in BCP 10. Normally six sitting members are appointed each year to sit for two years, and the IETF chair is appointed every two years. There is no limit on the number of terms, and mid-term vacancies do not affect the IAB's power to decide.
sections.eli5: The board has thirteen voting seats. The members are there as themselves, not to speak for their employers, and each year about half of the ordinary seats come up for renewal.

sections.title: Ex-Officio and Liaison Members
sections.content:
Ex-officio and liaison members may attend and join discussions but have no standing to take part in IAB decisions. An ex-officio position may be held by a full member, who then keeps the right to take part in decisions.

The IRTF chair and the IAB's Executive Director are ex-officio members. The Internet Society, the RFC Editor, the IANA and the IESG each appoint a liaison member, and these liaison positions may not be held by a full IAB member. Vacancies in these positions do not affect the IAB's power to take decisions.
sections.eli5: Some guests may sit at the table and talk but do not get to vote.

sections.title: What the IAB Is Responsible For
sections.content:
The IAB is chartered both as a committee of the IETF and as an advisory body of the Internet Society. The charter lists six responsibilities.

  • IESG appointment: the nominating committee provides candidates for vacant IESG seats and the IETF Chair, and the IAB consents to some, all or none.
  • Architectural oversight: oversight of the architecture of Internet protocols and procedures.
  • Standards process oversight and appeal: oversight of the process used to create Internet Standards, and acting as an appeal board for complaints of improper execution of that process.
  • RFC series and IANA: the IAB must approve the organization acting as RFC Editor and its general policy, and the organization acting as IANA.
  • ISOC liaison: advice and guidance to the Internet Society Board of Trustees and Officers on technical, architectural, procedural and, where appropriate, policy matters.
  • External liaison: representing the interests of the IETF and the Internet Society in technical liaison relationships with other organizations. Liaisons are kept as informal as possible and must be of demonstrable value.
sections.eli5: The board picks who can join the leadership team, keeps an eye on how the Internet fits together, makes sure the rules are followed, gives advice and talks to other groups.

sections.title: Architectural Oversight in Practice
sections.content:
A major role is long range planning and coordination between different areas of IETF activity. The IAB is expected to pay attention to important long-term issues and to bring them to the attention of groups able to address them.

Members watch emerging activities and Birds of a Feather sessions at IETF meetings. When a new working group is proposed, the IESG forwards a preliminary charter to the IAB, which reviews it for architectural consistency and integrity and gives feedback.

The IAB sponsors and organizes the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) and reviews proposed IRTF groups. It convenes invitational workshops for in-depth reviews of architectural issues, which produce a report that may advise the IETF community and the IESG. It may also organize ad hoc bodies of independent technical experts to adjudicate technical disputes.
sections.eli5: The board looks at new projects early to check they fit the big picture, holds special workshops on tricky topics and can ask outside experts to settle disagreements.

sections.title: How the IAB Is Organized
sections.content:
The members select one full member as IAB chair for a one-year term with no restriction on renewal. The chair can be removed by a two-thirds vote of the members, and manages the IAB's activities and meetings. The chair may appoint an honorary Executive Director for a one-year renewable term, who administers internal operation such as organizing meetings and reporting results.

The IAB appoints the IRTF chair for a two-year renewable term and can remove him or her. The IAB chair and another full member (not the IETF chair) serve as liaisons to the IESG, and the IESG appoints one of its members (not the IETF chair) as a liaison to the IAB.
sections.eli5: The board elects its own leader each year. The leader can pick an assistant to run the meetings, and the board also picks the head of the research group.

sections.title: Decisions, Openness and Confidentiality
sections.content:
The IAB tries to decide unanimously. If that fails, the chair may conduct informal polls to find consensus. The IAB may make decisions and take action if at least seven full members concur and there are no more than two dissents. Decisions may be reached in face to face meetings, by teleconference, by Internet communication, or any combination.

The IAB publishes minutes of all its meetings on the Internet and holds an open meeting at every IETF meeting. It publishes its findings as RFCs, Internet Drafts or messages to the IETF mailing list. Personnel matters and possibly legal and financial matters may be kept confidential, and the chair may, with the consent of the full members, exclude liaison and ex-officio members from those discussions.
sections.eli5: The board tries to agree on everything. If not, it can still act when at least seven members agree and no more than two object. Its minutes are public, except for a few private topics.

sections.title: Security and Changes from RFC 1601
sections.content:
The memo states that it does not raise any known security threats.

It replaces RFC 1601. The principal change is the removal of material now covered in BCP 8, BCP 9 and BCP 10, with many consequent editorial changes. Other changes: a description of decision making when unanimity cannot be achieved, a note on openness and confidentiality, new liaison seats for the Internet Society and the IANA, revised text on the IANA and the RFC Editor, and clarifications following legal review.
sections.eli5: The new rule book is shorter because other documents now explain some of the rules. It adds a way to decide without everyone agreeing, and new guest seats.
